deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up Hilbertian tensor and exterior powers. The likely purpose, judging from the next page, is Fredholm-determinant and Hadamard-type estimates (the 1953–56 work on nuclear operators and Fredholm theory). The previous page established that the Hilbert tensor product ⊗^{(2)} is functorial for bounded operators. It then defined a_n = (1/n!) Σ_σ ε_σ σ acting on the n-fold Hilbert tensor power of E.

This page:
(i) a_n is a hermitian projector. Each σ acts as a unitary operator, so a_n is continuous. The identity a_n² = a_n holds on the dense algebraic tensor product, hence everywhere. Hermitian symmetry follows from σ* = σ^{-1}. This in turn comes from (a_{σ1}⊗…⊗a_{σn}, b_1⊗…⊗b_n) = (a_1⊗…⊗a_n, b_{σ^{-1}1}⊗…⊗b_{σ^{-1}n}), a direct consequence of the definition (1) of the scalar product on decomposable tensors.
(ii) Definition: the Hilbertian n-th exterior power Λ^{n(2)}E is the image of a_n, with the scalar product multiplied by n!. Up to that factor it is the closed subspace a_n(⊗^{n(2)}E).
(iii) The algebraic exterior power Λ^nE injects naturally into it. Its image is a_n(algebraic ⊗^nE), which is dense. So Λ^{n(2)}E is the completion of Λ^nE for the induced scalar product.
(iv) Explicit formula on decomposables. Put A = a_1⊗…⊗a_n and B = b_1⊗…⊗b_n. Then (a_1∧…∧a_n, b_1∧…∧b_n) = n!(a_nA, a_nB) = n!(A, a_nB) = Σ_σ ε_σ Π(a_i, b_{σi}) = det((a_i, b_j)).

The next page states this as formula (4). It adds the theorem on existence and uniqueness of the positive hermitian form, and that the e_J form an orthonormal basis. It then derives the Gram/Hadamard inequality |det A| ≤ Π‖a_i‖ and the corollary |det(a_i, b_j)| ≤ Π‖a_i‖‖b_i‖. These are the tools for Fredholm-type determinant bounds.
errors: No mathematical error. The convention for how σ acts (σ versus σ^{-1}) is left implicit. The sign ε_σ is unaffected, so the determinant formula is correct.
Minor gap: continuity of a_n rests on each permutation operator being unitary. This is asserted ('car il est continu') rather than proved, though it follows from (1).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a textbook construction of Hilbert-space exterior powers and the Gram-determinant inner product, preparatory to Fredholm/Hadamard estimates. It is clean and correct, but entirely standard.
transcription_corrections: The exterior power notation is likely Λ̂^{n(2)}E or Λ^{(2)}E, following the '(2) = Hilbertian' convention used for ⊗^{(2)} on the previous page, rather than Λ̂^{(n)}E.
The tensor power should likely read ⊗^{n(2)}E (Hilbert tensor power) rather than ⊗̂^nE.
'dont l'image est identique à l'image de ⊗E' refers to the image under a_n of the algebraic tensor power ⊗^nE.
The line 'Cet espace s'identifie aussi à un sous-espace (au facteur n! près) de ⊗E image du projecteur a_n' is a parenthetical continuation of the definition.
